title: Trailing command args lose argv boundaries in launch resolution
description:
resolve_inner_command (launch.rs:194) and build_tmux_command (launch.rs:168-172) collapse the already-split trailing argv with trailing.join(" "). Args that contain spaces, quotes, globs, or $ are silently corrupted because the joined string is re-split by the downstream shell.

Example: 'title-preserver --dir ~/p -- vim "my file.txt"' resolves the inner command to 'exec vim my file.txt' — now two arguments instead of one. Same loss for the tmux path: 'tmux new -As dev vim my file.txt'.

This is the clear-cut half of the original #2/#3 review pair: trailing args arrive as structured argv and must stay structured. Fix: shell-quote each trailing arg (e.g. shell_words::quote / a small quoting helper) before joining, for both the bare-shell exec path and the tmux trailing path. Add tests with multi-word and metacharacter args.
acceptance_criteria: Trailing args containing spaces/quotes/globs survive resolution as single arguments; covered by unit tests; both the exec path and tmux-trailing path quote correctly.

title: Dry-run mode: print the resolved launch plan without spawning anything
description:
Confirmed no dry-run exists today: `main.rs:6-11` parses CLI, loads config, and calls straight into `proxy::run`, which resolves the command (`src/proxy.rs:155-180`) and immediately opens a PTY, enters raw terminal mode, spawns the child, and enters the retry loop. There is no way to see what *would* be run.

Add a `--dry-run` flag that resolves the full launch pipeline (shell + tmux + transport composition via the pure `LaunchConfig::resolve`, `src/launch.rs:418-442`) and prints the resulting `CommandSpec` (`src/session.rs:29-47`), then exits 0 — WITHOUT opening a PTY, touching terminal mode (no `ProxyRuntime::enter` / raw mode), spawning any child, installing signal handlers, or entering the retry loop. The dry-run path branches right after resolution in `proxy::run` (or in `main.rs`).

This doubles as a config/lint check: `LaunchConfig::validate` (`src/launch.rs:399-413`) still runs, so dry-run surfaces mutually-exclusive-flag errors and resolution failures before any side effects. It is also a preview of the *retry target*: the retry prompt re-runs this exact resolved command on `space`, so the printed plan is what a reconnect would execute — useful for the recovery work (`tipre-recovery-harness`, `tipre-reconnect-overlay`) and as the verification tool for user-injected flags (`tipre-extra-args`: "did my `--ssh-args`/`--tmux-args` land where I expected?").

OUTPUT FORMAT (open question)
- Default: a human-readable, shell-joined one-liner (reuse `shell_join`, `src/launch.rs:330-335`) — the thing you'd paste at a shell; print program and argv separately too.
- Optional machine-readable form (`--dry-run=json` or a separate `--json`) emitting the structured `CommandSpec` as JSON. Note `CommandSpec` is not currently `Serialize` (`src/session.rs:28-47`), so JSON output needs that derive added.
- Decide: one combined flag vs `--dry-run` + `--json`, and whether to also print the derived `LaunchContext` (transport kind + tmux target) so users can confirm e.g. that their remote tmux won't be sampled.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- `--dry-run` prints the resolved command and exits 0 with no PTY opened, no terminal-mode change, and no child spawned (assert no raw-mode entry).
- Config/validation errors still surface (dry-run of a mutually-exclusive-flag config exits non-zero with the existing error).
- Output is documented (README): the readable form by default, JSON form when requested, plus the `LaunchContext` summary if chosen.
- A test covers: local, ssh-transport, mosh-transport, and tmux invocations each print the expected resolved command (mirrors the `launch.rs` resolution tests).
- Coordinate with `tipre-extra-args` so the dry-run output reflects injected per-layer args.

title: Pass extra args to each managed layer (shell / tmux / ssh / mosh)
description:
Allow the user to inject extra flags into each command term-preserver composes, one flag family per managed layer: `--shell-args`, `--tmux-args`, `--ssh-args`, `--mosh-args`. Covers all the binaries term-preserver invokes today (shell, tmux, ssh, mosh), matching the inside-out composition in `src/launch.rs`.

INPUT FORMS (both must work)
- Repeated, one token each: `--ssh-args=-p --ssh-args=2222`
- Single occurrence, multiple tokens: `--ssh-args "-p 2222 -o ServerAliveInterval=5"`

Recommended semantics: each occurrence's value is shell-lexed (e.g. `shell-words`/`shlex` crate — check Cargo.toml first) into discrete argv tokens, and all tokens across all occurrences accumulate in order. Shell-lexing the multi-token form also lets embedded spaces survive via quotes (`--tmux-args "-X 'a b'"` → `[-X, "a b"]`), which a naive whitespace split cannot do. Tokens must be kept as a `Vec<String>` argv (not pre-joined) all the way through resolution, so the existing `shell_quote`/`shell_join` (`src/launch.rs:316-358`) can carry them intact across the ssh re-parse boundary.

INJECTION POINT (the main design question — needs care, differs per layer)
- ssh: alongside term-preserver's own `-t`, before the host: `ssh <user> -t host <cmd>`.
- mosh: before the host and its `--` terminator: `mosh <user> host -- ...`.
- tmux: among `new-session`/`attach-session` options — built-in flags (`-As`/`-s`/`-t`, `-c dir`) plus user flags, all before the trailing command (`src/launch.rs:201-221`). tmux is positional about options vs trailing command, so validate the chosen ordering against real tmux.
- shell: with the login/interactive flags, before `-c` (`src/launch.rs:237-312`). Shells treat post-`-c` args as positional, so user shell-args must land before `-c`.

OPEN QUESTIONS
- Conflicts with term-preserver's own emitted flags (e.g. user passes `--ssh-args=-t`, or `--tmux-args=-A` against attach mode): leave as-is and document, dedupe, or warn? Recommend leave-as-is + doc note.
- Config/env shape: add `shell_args`/`tmux_args`/`ssh_args`/`mosh_args` to `LaunchConfig` (`src/launch.rs:75-95`) as `Vec<String>`; in TOML as `[launch]` lists; env as JSON arrays (`TERM_PRESERVER_LAUNCH__TMUX_ARGS='["-d","-y"]'`), matching the existing `[launch]` pattern.
- Coordinate with the quoting tickets (`tipre-526`, `tipre-ahg`): args containing spaces/metachars must round-trip through launch resolution and the ssh shell-join; their survival is the acceptance bar.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- `--shell-args`/`--tmux-args`/`--ssh-args`/`--mosh-args` all exist, each accepts both the repeated-single-token form and the single-occurrence-multi-token form, and accumulate.
- Resolution tests (alongside the existing `launch.rs` tests) assert the injected tokens land at the correct per-layer position for local, ssh, and mosh transports — e.g. `--ssh-args "-p 2222"` with `--ssh w --tmux dev` yields `ssh -p 2222 -t w '... tmux new -As dev'`, and `--tmux-args=-d` places `-d` correctly in the tmux command.
- An arg containing a space survives launch resolution and the ssh `shell_join` boundary as one token (verified by test).
- New fields documented in the README launch table and the config-file/env sections.

title: Non-detach tmux attach: attach alongside existing clients without bumping them
description:
Goal: a deliberate, selectable attach policy where term-preserver attaches to a tmux session **alongside** any existing clients, never detaching ("bumping") them — the tmux equivalent of GNU screen's `screen -x` multi-display mode.

Current-state finding (this is mostly verify + make-explicit, not build-from-scratch): the commands `build_tmux_command` emits today already omit tmux's detach flags — `CreateOrAttach` → `tmux new -As <s>` and `Attach` → `tmux attach-session -t <s>` (`src/launch.rs:201-221`). In tmux, detaching other clients is opt-in via `-D` (on `new-session -A`) or `-d` (on `attach-session`). So the generated attach is already non-bumping *by omission*. This means the guarantee is currently emergent rather than intentional, named, or documented, and there is no way to request the opposite (take-over) behavior.

Why this matters for term-preserver specifically: in the mosh+tmux reconnect flow, when a link drops the *old* mosh/tmux client may still be alive (mosh keeps trying to reconnect for a long time). A respawn then attaches a second client. Non-detach means the new client joins the same session and the old one is left alone (so if the network recovers, both can coexist on the shared session); a take-over mode would kick the stale client. The right default and whether to expose the inverse is the real product decision here.

Mechanism mapping (tmux):
- non-detach (this ticket): `tmux new -As <s>` / `tmux attach-session -t <s>` (current).
- detach-others / take-over: `tmux new -ADs <s>` / `tmux attach-session -d -t <s>`.

OPEN QUESTIONS
- Confirm empirically (via `tipre-recovery-harness`) that the current command does not detach an existing client, so the guarantee is backed by a test, not just man-page reading.
- Default policy: keep non-detach as default and add an opt-in take-over flag (e.g. `--tmux-detach-others`), or expose a tri-state? Naming.
- Interaction with `--tmux` (create-or-attach) vs `--tmux-attach` (attach only): does the policy apply uniformly to both?
- mosh two-client case: is leaving the old client alive the behavior we want on reconnect? Coordinate with `tipre-reconnect-overlay`.
- Note: a user's own `~/.tmux.conf` (hooks, `detach-on-destroy`, etc.) can override attach behavior regardless of the flags term-preserver passes — out of scope to control, but worth a doc note.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- A test asserts the generated tmux command for the non-detach policy contains no `-D` (on `new`) and no `-d` (on `attach-session`), and that an existing attached client is not detached when a second term-preserver attach occurs (exercisable via `tipre-recovery-harness`).
- The non-detach policy is documented (README launch / tmux section) as the default attach behavior, with the screen `-x` analogy.
- A decision is recorded (in notes or a child ticket) on whether to add the inverse take-over mode; if added, its flag and generated commands are specified.

title: Status overlay on the last line: show reconnection status and time-until-reconnect
description:
When the child exits today, the proxy prints a static line and waits — potentially forever — for the user to press space (Retry prompt section of [`/README.md`](/README.md); `src/proxy.rs:82-99`). There is no visible indication of *when* a reconnect will happen, and no automatic reconnect: recovery is purely manual. (Confirming the open question: term-preserver does **not** currently reconnect automatically; `PromptPolicy::decide_key` only retries on an explicit `space` keystroke — `src/prompt.rs:24-31`.)

This ticket adds a visual overlay anchored to the last screen line that surfaces, at minimum:
- current status (child exited / waiting / reconnecting), and
- time until reconnection.

This implies deciding and implementing an **automatic-reconnect policy with a countdown**, since a "time until reconnection" only makes sense if reconnection happens on its own. The overlay must coexist with the existing prompt text and, importantly, must respect the screen-preservation guarantee validated in `tipre-screen-preserve` — i.e. it should repaint only its own line(s), not erase the screen above it. Likely a fixed bottom line (save/restore cursor, clear line, repaint on each tick) driven by the existing poll loop in `read_prompt_input` (`src/proxy.rs:131-153`).

Open questions to resolve (split into child tickets if needed):
- Auto-reconnect policy: fixed backoff? configurable delay? opt-in vs default? Should manual `space` still skip the countdown and retry immediately?
- What counts as "reconnection" for the countdown — respawn of the resolved command (current retry semantics), or something mosh-aware?
- Does the overlay replace the current static prompt line or sit below it?

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- After a child exit, a status overlay renders on the last screen line showing reconnection status and a live time-until-reconnect, updating at least once per second without disturbing screen content above it (verified against `tipre-screen-preserve`'s no-clear test).
- Reconnection occurs automatically per the chosen policy without a keystroke; manual `space` still triggers an immediate retry.
- Overlay rendering and the countdown are exercisable via `tipre-recovery-harness` (no real network needed).
- The overlay is cleaned up (line cleared / cursor restored) on both retry and quit so the next session starts clean.

title: Validate that screen content is preserved across child exit and respawn
description:
The retry-prompt docs state the proxy "keeps the screen contents" on child exit and appends the prompt below (see Retry prompt section of [`/README.md`](/README.md)). The mechanism is implicit: the proxy never emits a screen-clear / cursor-home sequence at the exit boundary — it only writes a leading CRLF then the prompt (`src/prompt.rs:36-38`, `src/proxy.rs:103-128`). But this guarantee is not asserted anywhere, and "screen content is preserved" can mean several things that need pinning down:

1. On child exit, the outer terminal's visible screen is not erased/scrolled/rewritten beyond appending the prompt line. (Proxy-side guarantee.)
2. Across a respawn (space → new `ChildSession`), the *new* child's screen reconstructs. This is only true when the child itself recovers its screen — mosh does; a plain shell or ssh does not. The proxy does not capture or replay screen text today (only OSC title/color state via `--reemit-title`).

This ticket is initially **validation**, not necessarily implementation: using the recovery harness (`tipre-recovery-harness`), confirm whether (1) actually holds — i.e. that nothing in `write_post_exit_output` or the relay teardown emits bytes that disturb the existing screen. If it holds, encode the guarantee as a regression test. If a violation is found (a stray clear, alternate-screen exit, or scroll), convert this ticket to a fix.

Scope note: (2) — preserving visible screen *text* across a respawn for non-mosh children — is a much larger feature (screen-text capture/replay) and is explicitly out of scope here; this ticket only validates the proxy-side no-clear guarantee and pins down what "preserved" means. Open question to resolve while validating: is OSC re-emit (`--reemit-title`) the only state that should cross the boundary, or is there an expectation that visible text survives too? Record the answer in notes.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- Using `tipre-recovery-harness`, an automated test asserts that the bytes the proxy writes at the exit boundary contain no screen-clearing control sequences (no `\x1b[2J`, no `\x1b[H` erase, no `\x1b[?1049l` alternate-screen switch introduced by the proxy itself) — only the CRLF + prompt (and optional gone/reemit lines).
- A short note (ticket notes or `doc/`) records what "screen content preserved" means for term-preserver: proxy-side no-clear is guaranteed; cross-respawn text reconstruction is the child's job (mosh yes, plain shell no).
- If validation finds a violation, the ticket is reclassified as a bug and the offending emission is fixed.

title: Recovery test harness: drive the failure → prompt → retry path without a flaky link
description:
Today the only way to exercise term-preserver's failure-and-recovery flow — child exits, the `[term-preserver] child exited...` prompt appears, the user presses space to respawn the same resolved command — is to kill a real child (often a live mosh/ssh link) by hand. That is slow, nondeterministic, and makes it impossible to write automated assertions about what hits the outer terminal at the exit boundary (whether the screen is cleared, whether OSC state is re-emitted, whether a future reconnect overlay renders correctly).

We need a deterministic, local way to drive the proxy through the failure → prompt → retry loop with no network and no human keystrokes, so that screen/byte-level behavior at the exit boundary becomes observable and assertable. This unblocks validation of screen-content preservation (`tipre-screen-preserve`) and development of the reconnect overlay (`tipre-reconnect-overlay`).

"Non-fast recovery" is the framing: mosh gives transparent *fast* recovery inside the child; what we want to test is the *non-fast* path the proxy itself owns — the proxy's own exit boundary and retry prompt, where recovery is manual today (and, later, automatic with a countdown).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- A reproducible, local-only way exists to drive term-preserver through at least one full failure → prompt → retry cycle with no real ssh/mosh connection and no human at the keyboard. Candidates to evaluate (pick the lightest that works): an integration test that spawns term-preserver against a fake child that exits on a byte/signal, or a debug flag like `--debug-exit-after <ms>` / `--debug-child <spec>` that makes a real run die on cue.
- The harness exposes (for assertion or inspection) the exact bytes written to the outer terminal around the exit boundary, so screen-clearing, prompt text, and (later) overlay rendering can be checked.
- The harness can deliver a synthetic `space` (retry) keystroke to drive a respawn and observe the second session.
- Documented in the README or `doc/` as the canonical way to reproduce the recovery flow for debugging.

title: Resampling policy: event-driven and final-at-exit refresh for tmux state
description:
The base sampler refreshes on a fixed 20s interval (kept as the floor). Add resampling triggers for freshness and a robust exit sample:

- Final resample at child exit: attempt one last `sample_once` before snapshotting into `SessionExit`, falling back to the cached last sample when the tmux server/client is already gone. The primary use case is the tmux server going away on exit — the cached sample is the robust path, but a best-effort fresh sample right after `child.wait()` (before the client fully detaches) tightens accuracy. This also makes the gone-line / `SessionExit.tmux` reliable for end-to-end testing, which the current poll timing makes flaky (the immediate sample races client registration).
- Event-driven resample: a captured title change (OSC 0/1/2) often signals a context switch; use it as a hint to resample sooner than the interval. Likewise resample on SIGWINCH.
- Adaptive interval: back off toward the 20s floor when consecutive samples are identical; tighten after a change.
- On-demand resample: expose a `TmuxState::refresh_now()`-style hook for future live-status display.

Base interval stays 20s. Coordinate with tipre-tmux-session-id (the poll sampler) and tipre-tmux-control-mode (control mode would obsolete event-driven polling).
acceptance_criteria: Child exit produces a `SessionExit.tmux` that is either a fresh final sample or the last cached sample, deterministically (no race with client registration). An OSC title-change triggers a resample sooner than the 20s floor. Interval backs off when state is stable. An end-to-end test (proxy launching a local tmux session) asserts the gone line carries a tmux session id without a 20s wait.

title: Track tmux state reactively via control mode (tmux -C) instead of polling
description:
The landed sampler (tipre-tmux-session-id) polls the local tmux server every ~20s. tmux control mode (the `tmux -C` client flag) switches tmux to a line-oriented protocol where it emits `%`-prefixed events for every state change — `%session-window-changed`, `%window-renamed`, `%pane-mode-changed`, `%client-session-changed`, `%layout-change`, etc. Subscribing to that stream keeps the tracked session/pane state always-fresh with zero polling cost and no up-to-20s staleness.

Lean on existing control-mode implementations rather than hand-rolling the `%`-line parser: `promptctl` and `tmux-control-mode-js`. Evaluate fit for a Rust project — likely extract/port the wire-protocol parsing rather than take a JS dependency; if no Rust crate exists, the `%`-line grammar is small enough to own.

Implementation shape: a control-mode client thread that opens a control client against the target session (`tmux -C -L <socket>` / `new-client -C`), reads `%`-lines, updates `TmuxState` in place, and exits when the child exits. The poll-based `TmuxSampler` (tmux.rs) stays as a fallback when control mode is unavailable or for remote sessions.

Remote: control mode speaks to a tmux server; a remote tmux (over ssh/mosh) would need the control client run on the remote host with its `%`-lines tunneled back — ties into the remote-introspection gap (`LaunchContext.local_tmux_target()` currently yields `None` for any transport).

Coordinate with tipre-tmux-session-id (poll sampler) and tipre-tmux-resample.
acceptance_criteria: A control-mode client updates TmuxState within sub-second of real tmux state changes (no 20s staleness), gated behind availability; poll sampler remains as fallback. `%`-line parsing unit-tested against recorded fixtures; integration test asserts freshness against a live server. No dependency decision is presumed — record the chosen approach (port vs crate vs own) in the ticket notes.

title: Track tmux session id per window and what is attached inside
description: On child exit, surface the tmux session id for each window and what is attached inside it (the inner process), alongside the existing exit dump (title, pid, observed OSC state). The launch config already knows the --tmux session name we asked for, but the *actual* attached session id and the process inside the pane require runtime introspection (e.g. querying the tmux server via tmux display-message / list-panes), which is out of scope for the color/icon slots change. This enables a richer 'gone' exit dump: title + pid + tmux session id + inner command.
acceptance_criteria: Exit dump (visible print and/or SessionExit) includes the live tmux session id for the window the proxy launched, and the command/process attached inside the pane, queried at runtime rather than assumed from --tmux. Coordinate with tipre-print-gone-title.

title: Capture and log sixel graphics as a tracked slot
description: Track sixel graphics sequences (DCS ... q ...) emitted by the child as a first-class observed slot, mirroring how OSC title/icon/color are captured. Stretch/super-overkill per initial scoping: capture image data (e.g. as scanlines or an in-memory raster) so the proxy can preserve or re-emit graphical state, or at minimum record that a sixel image was emitted and its dimensions.
acceptance_criteria: Sixel DCS sequences are recognized and either captured structurally (dimensions + pixel data) or at minimum counted/surfaced via observed state and SessionExit. Out of scope for the initial color/icon slots work; ticketed here so the slot is not forgotten.

title: Track icon name (OSC 1) separately from window title
description:
OSC 1 (icon name) is currently captured into the same `current_title` slot as OSC 0/2 (window title) — see `osc1_captures_icon_title` (osc.rs:151). The icon name is conflated with the window title: a later OSC 2 overwrites an earlier OSC 1 and vice versa, all stored in one field. Per the xterm spec, OSC 0 sets BOTH icon and window, OSC 1 sets icon only, OSC 2 sets window only. Separate icon-name state from window-title state so each can be preserved and re-emitted independently, mirroring the title-preservation model.

Implementation notes:
- `TitleObserver.current_title` (osc.rs:19,115) holds the last of ANY OSC 0/1/2. Split into `window_title` (OSC 2, and OSC 0) and `icon_name` (OSC 1, and OSC 0). OSC 0 writes both.
- `SessionExit.last_title` (session.rs:87) becomes two fields (or a small struct), and the retry loop re-emit path (proxy.rs:77-79, prompt::title_reemit_sequence) emits both OSC 1 and OSC 2 sequences on restore.
- Coordinate with tipre-print-gone-title (window-title visible record) so icon gets a parallel story, and with tipre-keep-color-osc on the shared re-emit plumbing.
acceptance_criteria: Icon name (OSC 1) and window title (OSC 2) tracked as distinct state. On re-emit, both restored; OSC 0 sets both. Unit tests in osc.rs verify independence (OSC 2 does not clobber a prior OSC 1 and vice versa); integration tests in tests/relay.rs cover re-emit of each.
close_reason: Landed: icon name (OSC 1) tracked separately from window title (OSC 2); OSC 0 sets both. Distinct slots in ObservedSlots, re-emitted independently.

title: Preserve terminal color OSC (4, 10/11/12) across child exit
description:
The OSC observer (osc.rs) currently recognizes only OSC 0/1/2 as title sequences; everything else is parsed past and discarded. OSC 4 (color palette) is literally the negative-case test `non_title_osc_does_not_change_title` (osc.rs:158). Extend the observer to capture color-setting sequences so the proxy can preserve and re-emit terminal color state, mirroring the title-preservation model.

Color OSC sequences in scope:
- OSC 4;N;SPEC — set palette color N (e.g. `4;0;rgb:aa/bb/cc`, `4;1;#aabbcc`)
- OSC 10;SPEC / 11;SPEC / 12;SPEC — default foreground / background / cursor color (optional stretch)

Implementation notes:
- `finish_osc` keys only on param 0/1/2 (osc.rs:95). Add param 4 (and optionally 10/11/12).
- OSC 4 data carries index + spec separated by `;`. Today `osc_param` captures only the first digit run up to the first `;` and `osc_data` swallows the rest, so for OSC 4 param is "4" and data is "N;SPEC" — needs sub-parsing on `;`.
- Store captured colors in a map (palette index -> spec) on the observer, plus optional fg/bg/cursor slots.
- Surface via SessionExit (session.rs:87) so the retry loop can re-emit on child exit, parallel to last_title (proxy.rs:77-79). Re-emit reconstructs the OSC sequence from captured state.
- Keep orthogonal to reemit_title (invisible restore) and the print-gone-title (visible record) features — color restoration is invisible like re-emit.
acceptance_criteria: OSC 4 palette sequences are captured by the observer and re-emitted on child exit when a color-preserve flag is set; OSC 10/11/12 optional. Unit tests in osc.rs cover capture of palette entries (including rgb: and #hex specs); integration test in tests/relay.rs covers re-emit alongside existing title cases.
close_reason: Landed: OSC 4 palette (multi-pair) + OSC 10/11/12 fg/bg/cursor captured into ObservedSlots with parsed 24-bit RGB; re-emitted on exit.

title: Print "gone <title>" on child exit
description:
When the child process exits, print the last captured OSC title as visible text in the format `gone <title>` (e.g. `gone user@host: ~/src`).

This is distinct from the existing `--reemit-title` flag, which re-emits the invisible OSC 2 escape sequence to re-set the terminal title. That keeps the title alive; this feature surfaces the title as human-readable text at the exit/prompt boundary, signaling that the process which owned that title is now gone.

Implementation notes:
- The last title is already tracked: `TitleObserver::current_title()` (osc.rs:115) flows into `SessionExit.last_title` (session.rs:87), and the retry loop already inspects `exit.last_title` in proxy.rs:77-79 for the re-emit path.
- Natural emission point is alongside the retry prompt in `RetryLoop` (proxy.rs), after the re-emit check, before/with the `[term-preserver] child exited...` line.
- Decide gating: a new flag (e.g. `--print-title`) vs always-on vs coupled to `--reemit-title`. Lean toward a dedicated flag so re-emit (invisible title restoration) and print (visible record) stay orthogonal.
acceptance_criteria: On child exit with a captured title present, the proxy prints `gone <title>` to stdout. With no title captured, nothing (or a `gone` with empty/sentinel) is printed — exact behavior to be decided. Behavior is gated by an opt-in flag distinct from `--reemit-title`. Covered by integration tests in tests/relay.rs alongside the existing reemit cases.
close_reason: Landed: --print-gone-title prints 'gone <title> (pid N)' at the exit boundary (prompt::format_gone_line, proxy::RetryLoop::write_post_exit_output).

title: Decide and document quoting vs shell-expansion policy for --dir and tmux session names
description:
dir (cd {d}) and tmux session names (tmux new -As {session}) are interpolated raw into shell strings (launch.rs). Unlike trailing args, --dir intentionally relies on shell evaluation so that ~ and $VAR expand — naive quoting would break that feature. So this needs a deliberate policy, not a blanket quote.

Decide per field:
- --dir: keep shell-evaluated (document that ~, $VAR, globs are expanded by the shell; spaces require user escaping), OR quote and lose expansion, OR expand ~ ourselves and quote the rest.
- tmux session name: tmux names are restrictive but a name with a space/'.' currently breaks; decide whether to quote.

Then document the chosen semantics in the README launcher section so users know what is and isn't shell-evaluated. Pairs with the trailing-arg boundary bug (separate ticket) which is an unambiguous fix.
acceptance_criteria: A documented decision for --dir and tmux-name handling; README states which fields are shell-evaluated vs literal; behavior matches the doc.

title: Integration tests for launch resolution scenarios
description:
The launch pipeline (launch.rs) is well unit-tested at the string-builder level, but nothing exercises resolve() end-to-end against real processes, and nothing covers the interesting cross-cutting scenarios. Add integration tests (tests/launch.rs) that spawn real children where feasible and assert on resolved CommandSpec for the rest.

Scenarios worth covering:
- Local tmux create-or-attach actually starts and the proxy relays it (gated on tmux present).
- Remote-shaped resolution: --ssh host --tmux dev produces ssh -t ... and --mosh host --tmux dev (assert CommandSpec, no network).
- --dir with ~ and $VAR expansion: confirm the cd layer is shell-evaluated as intended.
- Trailing command with multiple args and an arg containing a space/quote (ties to the quoting tickets).
- Each shell family: posix (zsh/bash/sh), fish, nushell bare + with inner + with dir.
- Fallback snippet path: unset $SHELL, no --shell.
- no-login/no-interactive combinations.
- Mutual-exclusivity errors surface (--ssh+--mosh, multiple --tmux*).
- Config-file + env + CLI precedence for [launch] fields.

Prefer asserting on the resolved CommandSpec for portability; gate any real-spawn tests behind presence checks (tmux/fish/nu) so CI without them still passes.
acceptance_criteria: tests/launch.rs exists; covers the scenarios above; real-spawn tests gated on tool availability; cargo test green on a machine without tmux/fish/nu (those tests skip/ignore cleanly).

title: CLI/config integration and command resolution pipeline
description:
Wire session-launching flags through figment2 config loading, resolve into final CommandSpec before session startup.

## CLI parsing

New flags added to CliArgs (clap derive):
- --shell <name>
- --ssh <host>
- --mosh <host>
- --tmux <session>
- --tmux-create <session>
- --tmux-attach <session>
- --dir <path>
- --no-login (flag)
- --no-interactive (flag)

Trailing -- command args still supported as innermost layer.

## Resolution pipeline

The SessionLaunchSpec (all the flags above) resolves into CommandSpec via:

1. Determine shell (launcher-shell ticket)
2. Build tmux command if any tmux flag (launcher-tmux ticket)
3. Determine inner command: trailing args > tmux command > None
4. Build shell invocation (launcher-shell ticket)
5. Wrap in transport if ssh/mosh (launcher-transport ticket)
6. Result: CommandSpec consumed by existing retry loop

## Trailing args interaction

If trailing -- command present AND tmux flags present:
- Trailing command runs INSIDE tmux session
- inner_cmd becomes: tmux new -As <session>  # then user command runs inside via tmux default-command? 
Actually: tmux runs the shell, shell sources rc, then user's trailing command runs.
This needs careful thought during implementation.

If trailing command present WITHOUT tmux:
- inner_cmd becomes the trailing command directly
- Shell wraps: zsh -lic 'exec <trailing>'

## Config integration

New fields in Config or a separate SessionLaunchConfig struct:
- launch_shell: Option<String>
- launch_ssh: Option<String>
- launch_mosh: Option<String>
- launch_tmux: Option<TmuxMode>  (enum: CreateOrAttach/Create/Attach with session name)
- launch_dir: Option<String>
- launch_login: bool (default true)
- launch_interactive: bool (default true)

Loaded via figment2 with same precedence: CLI > env > TOML > defaults.

## Retry behavior

RetryLoop already re-runs the resolved CommandSpec. Since CommandSpec includes the full stack (ssh/mosh + shell + tmux), retry reconnects and re-attaches. No changes needed to retry loop.

## Env var support

TITLE_PROXY_LAUNCH_SSH=w
TITLE_PROXY_LAUNCH_TMUX=compfuzor
TITLE_PROXY_LAUNCH_DIR=~/src/foo
TITLE_PROXY_LAUNCH_LOGIN=false

## Testing

Integration tests: verify resolved CommandSpec for various flag combinations. Test config file loading of launch fields. Test env var overrides.
notes:
## --dir without tmux (clarified)

When --dir is specified without tmux flags, the inner command is cd + exec shell:

  title-proxy --dir ~/src/foo
  → zsh -lic 'cd ~/src/foo && exec zsh -li'

  title-proxy --ssh w --dir ~/src/foo
  → ssh w -- zsh -lic 'cd ~/src/foo && exec zsh -li'

Starts an interactive shell from inside the target directory.

## --dir with trailing command but no tmux

  title-proxy --dir ~/src/foo -- make test
  → zsh -lic 'cd ~/src/foo && exec make test'
Implemented. CliArgs has 9 new flags (--shell, --ssh, --mosh, --tmux, --tmux-create, --tmux-attach, --dir, --no-login, --no-interactive). CliOverlay uses nested LaunchOverlay for figment2. proxy::run uses is_active guard to choose between launch resolution and legacy CommandSpec path. 7 new config tests covering CLI parsing and defaults.

title: Remote transport flags (--ssh, --mosh)
description:
Parse remote transport flags, enforce mutual exclusivity, wrap command vector in transport layer.

## Flags (mutually exclusive -- error if both specified)

- --ssh <host>: wraps command in SSH transport
- --mosh <host>: wraps command in mosh transport

## Wrapping

Given a resolved shell command vector, produce the transport-wrapped vector:
- SSH: [ssh, <host>, --, ...shell_cmd]
- mosh: [mosh, <host>, --, ...shell_cmd]
- Neither: shell_cmd (unchanged)

## Example

Shell cmd: [zsh, -lic, 'exec tmux new -As dev']
With --ssh w: [ssh, w, --, zsh, -lic, 'exec tmux new -As dev']
With --mosh w: [mosh, w, --, zsh, -lic, 'exec tmux new -As dev']

## --dir on remote

--dir refers to the REMOTE filesystem when ssh/mosh is active. The shell wrapping handles cd on the remote side.

## Testing

Pure unit tests. Test ssh wrapping, mosh wrapping, mutual exclusivity error, no-transport passthrough.
notes: Implemented in src/launch.rs. wrap_transport wraps in ssh/mosh. Mutual exclusivity validated. All tested.

title: Tmux session flags and command construction
description:
Parse tmux-related flags, enforce mutual exclusivity, build tmux command strings.

## Flags (mutually exclusive -- fail if multiple specified)

- --tmux <session>: create-or-attach → tmux new -As <session>
- --tmux-create <session>: create only → tmux new -s <session>
- --tmux-attach <session>: attach only → tmux a -t <session>

## --dir integration

When --dir is specified alongside tmux:
- create-or-attach: tmux new -c <dir> -As <session>
- create: tmux new -c <dir> -s <session>
- attach: tmux attach-session -c <dir> -t <session> (tmux 3.0+)

When --dir is specified WITHOUT tmux: handled by shell layer (cd wrapping).

## Output

Produces an optional tmux command string (e.g. 'tmux new -c ~/src/foo -As dev') that becomes the inner command for the shell invocation builder.

If no tmux flags specified: None (shell runs bare or with trailing command).

## Testing

Pure unit tests. Test all three modes, --dir integration, mutual exclusivity error cases.
notes:
## Trailing command + tmux (clarified)

Trailing args become tmux's command argument natively:

  title-proxy --mosh w --tmux dev -- vim
  → mosh w -- zsh -lic 'exec tmux new -As dev vim'

tmux handles this correctly — vim runs inside the new/attached session.
Implemented in src/launch.rs. TmuxMode enum with CreateOrAttach/Create/Attach. Dir handled via tmux -c flag. Trailing args become tmux command argument. All tested.

title: Shell family detection and invocation builder
description:
Pure functional core: detect shell family from name/path, build shell invocation vectors.

## Shell families

| Family | Shells | Login+command | Bare login+interactive |
|--------|--------|---------------|------------------------|
| POSIX | bash, zsh, sh, dash | <shell> -lc 'exec <cmd>' | <shell> -li |
| fish | fish | fish -lc 'exec <cmd>' | fish -li |
| nushell | nu, nushell | nu -c '<cmd>' | nu |

Nushell has no -l flag and no exec builtin; nu -c exits after running.

## Shell fallback chain

1. --shell flag value (if provided)
2. $SHELL env var basename
3. zsh (if it exists on PATH)
4. sh

Detection takes the basename of the path (handles /bin/zsh, /usr/bin/zsh, zsh all mapping to zsh).

## Flags

- --shell <name>: explicit override, accepts full path or basename
- --no-login: skip -l (default: login)
- --no-interactive: skip -i (default: interactive)

## Invocation builder

Given a shell name, login/interactive booleans, and optional inner command, produce Vec<String>:
- No inner command: [shell, (-l if login), (-i if interactive)]
- With inner command (POSIX/fish): [shell, (-l), (-i), -c, 'exec <inner>']
- With inner command (nu): [nu, -c, '<inner>']

## Testing

Pure unit tests, no I/O. Test all three families, login/interactive combos, fallback chain.
notes:
## Fallback resolution (clarified)

For the no-information case (no --shell, no $SHELL), emit a portable runtime snippet rather than checking PATH locally:

- Without inner command: sh -c 'command -v zsh >/dev/null 2>&1 && exec zsh -li || exec sh -li'
- With inner command: sh -c 'if command -v zsh >/dev/null 2>&1; then exec zsh -lic "exec <inner>"; else exec sh -lc "exec <inner>"; fi'

This works locally and remotely without needing to probe the target filesystem before connecting. sh is guaranteed on any Unix; the snippet promotes to zsh at runtime if available.

The resolution chain becomes:
1. --shell flag → use directly
2. $SHELL → use directly
3. Neither → emit runtime detection snippet via sh -c
## Updated per design doc resolutions

Shell fallback now respects remote $SHELL. Updated chain:
1. --shell flag → use directly (no existence check, pass through)
2. $SHELL env var → use directly
3. Runtime snippet via sh -c that checks $SHELL on the target, then zsh, then sh:
   sh -c 'if [ -n "$SHELL" ]; then exec "$SHELL" -li; elif command -v zsh >/dev/null 2>&1; then exec zsh -li; else exec sh -li; fi'

No local PATH checks. The snippet runs on the target machine (local or remote).

See doc/design/2026-06-22-session-launcher.md for full pipeline architecture.
Implemented in src/launch.rs. 50 tests covering shell family detection, flags, invocation builder (POSIX/fish/nu), fallback snippet, and dir handling.

title: Session launching flags for composable remote/tmux/shell commands
description:
title-proxy currently accepts a single trailing command vector. This epic adds composable convenience flags that resolve into a single CommandSpec before session startup.

## Flags

- --shell <name>: shell override (default: $SHELL basename, fallback zsh-then-sh)
- --ssh <host>: SSH transport (mutually exclusive with --mosh)
- --mosh <host>: mosh transport (mutually exclusive with --ssh)
- --tmux <session>: create-or-attach (tmux new -As)
- --tmux-create <session>: create only (tmux new -s)
- --tmux-attach <session>: attach only (tmux a -t)
- --dir <path>: working directory for innermost layer
- --no-login: skip login shell mode
- --no-interactive: skip interactive shell mode

## Composition model

Flags build the command vector inside-out: shell (innermost) -> optional tmux wraps inside shell -> optional ssh/mosh wraps everything.

Example: title-proxy --mosh w --tmux compfuzor
Resolves to: mosh w -- zsh -lic 'exec tmux new -As compfuzor'

## Key decisions

- --tmux defaults to create-or-attach; --tmux-create/--tmux-attach are explicit; fail if multiple specified
- --ssh and --mosh mutually exclusive
- Default: login + interactive shell (-li for POSIX) for full env setup
- Shell fallback: --shell > $SHELL > zsh (if exists) > sh
- Trailing -- command runs as innermost layer
- Retry re-runs fully resolved CommandSpec (reconnects, re-attaches)
notes:
## Architecture finalized

See doc/design/2026-06-22-session-launcher.md for the full design.

Key shape: LaunchConfig nested in Config (not a standalone spec). Pure resolution pipeline in launch.rs with 4 stages: resolve_shell → resolve_inner_command → build_shell_invocation → wrap_transport.

Implementation order: tickets 1-3 (shell/tmux/transport) are all pure functions in launch.rs, can be built together. Ticket 4 (config integration) wires them to CLI/config/proxy.

tmux 3.0+ baseline (for attach-session -c). Shell pass-through, no existence check. Remote $SHELL fallback in detection snippet.
All child tickets complete. launch.rs has 50 tests, config.rs has 7 new launch tests. Full suite 97 tests passing, clippy clean.
